title: Monomorphic VT
teach: Regular wide-complex tachycardia: VT until proven otherwise. Unstable: synchronised cardioversion. Stable: amiodarone or procainamide. Never verapamil.

title: Ventricular fibrillation
teach: No organised QRS. Cardiac arrest: start CPR and defibrillate now.

title: Torsades de pointes
teach: Polymorphic VT twisting around the baseline on a long QT. IV magnesium; defibrillate if pulseless; stop QT-prolonging drugs.

title: Anterior STEMI (LAD)
teach: ST elevation V1–V4 (and I, aVL) with reciprocal inferior depression: anterior STEMI from the LAD. Reperfuse now.

title: Inferior STEMI (RCA)
teach: ST elevation II, III, aVF (III > II) with reciprocal depression in aVL: inferior STEMI. Record V4R; reperfuse now.

title: Posterior MI
teach: Horizontal ST depression V1–V3 with tall R waves: posterior MI seen from the front. Record V7–V9; treat as STEMI.

title: De Winter T waves
teach: Upsloping ST depression into tall symmetrical precordial T waves: de Winter, a proximal LAD occlusion. Cath lab now.

title: Wellens syndrome
teach: Deep symmetrical T inversion V2–V3 in a pain-free patient: Wellens, critical LAD stenosis. Admit for early angiography; no stress test.

title: Diffuse ST depression, aVR elevation
teach: Widespread ST depression with ST elevation in aVR: global subendocardial ischaemia (left main or 3-vessel disease, or demand). Urgent angiography if chest pain.

title: Complete heart block
teach: P waves and QRS complexes march independently; slow wide escape. Complete heart block: pacing pads on, arrange pacing.

title: Mobitz I (Wenckebach)
teach: PR lengthens until a beat drops: Wenckebach, usually AV-nodal and benign. Review drugs; pace only if symptomatic.

title: Mobitz II
teach: Constant PR with sudden dropped beats, often with a wide QRS: Mobitz II. High risk of complete block; pacing.

title: Hyperkalaemia
teach: Peaked T, flat P and widening QRS: hyperkalaemia. IV calcium now, then insulin-dextrose and salbutamol, then remove K+.

title: Hypokalaemia
teach: Flat T, prominent U and ST sag: hypokalaemia. Replace K+ and check Mg2+.

title: Long QT
teach: QTc well over 500 ms: high torsades risk. Stop QT drugs, correct K+ and Mg2+.

title: AV nodal re-entry (AVNRT)
teach: Regular narrow tachycardia with hidden P waves: AVNRT. Modified Valsalva, then adenosine; cardiovert if unstable.

title: AF with rapid ventricular response
teach: AF at 130–160/min. Look for the driver (sepsis, hypovolaemia, thyroid); rate control if stable; cardiovert if unstable.

title: Atrial flutter, 2:1
teach: Sawtooth F waves with 2:1 block at 150/min. Rate control or cardioversion; anticoagulate as for AF.

title: Brugada pattern, type 1
teach: Coved ST elevation in V1–V2 with T inversion: Brugada type 1. Treat fever, avoid sodium-channel blockers, refer for EP.

title: Acute pericarditis
teach: Diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression and no reciprocal change: pericarditis. NSAID with colchicine; echo.

title: Wolff–Parkinson–White
teach: Short PR and delta wave. Avoid AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF; refer for ablation.

title: Hypothermia
teach: Osborn J waves with bradycardia and long QT: hypothermia. Rewarm gently; the cold heart fibrillates easily.

title: Pulmonary embolism
teach: Sinus tachycardia with S1Q3T3 and right-sided T inversion: right heart strain. Score probability; CTPA; the ECG cannot exclude PE.

title: Sinus bradycardia
teach: Sinus bradycardia. Symptoms and blood pressure decide urgency, not the number.

title: Sinus tachycardia
teach: Sinus tachycardia: find and treat the cause.

title: Normal sinus rhythm
teach: Normal sinus rhythm: the reference tracing.

title: Left bundle branch block
teach: Broad notched R in the lateral leads, QS in V1, discordant ST-T: LBBB. New LBBB with chest pain and instability: treat as STEMI equivalent (Sgarbossa).

title: Junctional rhythm
teach: Narrow QRS at 40–60/min with inverted P close to the QRS: junctional rhythm. Look for drugs, digoxin, inferior MI.
